title: Add smoke eval coverage and auto-regressions for config-driven model rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: A recent configuration-driven model variant rollout caused a subtle quality regression on a subset of customer prompt families. The incident surfaced because the broader eval pipeline did not include targeted smoke coverage for the changed config flags and the canary traffic was too small to detect delta metrics. This ticket captures the design and implementation of a compact, fast "smoke eval" suite that runs automatically on config/model changes and a lightweight auto-regression gating system for rollouts. Goals: (1) detect ≥5% relative regression in any tracked metric for a prompt-family within 10 minutes of rollout, (2) require gating for rollouts that change inference config or model family, (3) keep runtime < 30s and cost minimal so it runs on PRs and canary waves.
acceptance_criteria: A compact smoke eval suite (<=200 queries) covering high-risk prompt families is executable as a CI job and as a post-deploy canary job.
The smoke eval runs automatically when a change touches inference-config or model pin in repo, and on canary deployment triggers.
An auto-regression check flags rollouts if any tracked metric regresses beyond configured thresholds and can optionally block automated promotion.
Dashboards show per-prompt-family delta, baseline distribution, and an actionable alert with example counterfactuals.
Documentation for runbook and developer guidance is published and linked in the rollout process.
timeline: 2026-03-10 - Incident triage: identified config rollouts as vector; collected failing prompts and metrics (Ava C.).
2026-03-11 - Spike: ran selective prompt families across model variants to characterize failure modes (Luis R., Priya K.).
2026-03-12 - Design review: proposed smoke eval size, metrics to track, and CI gating flow; reviewed with SRE and PM (design signoff).
actions: Create a canonical compact prompt family set: extract 120-180 queries prioritized by customer impact and past regression sensitivity.
Implement smoke-eval runner in eval-service with tuning to run in <30s (parallelization + small batch sizes).
Hook smoke-eval to config change CI: detect diffs in inference-config/* and model registry changes; run smoke-eval as required job.
Add a canary post-deploy hook that runs the smoke-eval against the canary model variant and compare to baseline.
Create auto-regression check logic: compute relative change, apply per-family thresholds, and emit pass/fail to rollout controller.
Ship dashboards and an alerting rule (PagerDuty for P0 regressions, Slack channel for P1) with example counterfactuals.
tests_to_add: Unit tests for smoke-eval CLI and parsing of results
Integration test that exercises smoke-eval in CI with a synthetic model variant
E2E canary test: deploy a toy config change in staging and verify auto-blocking behavior
Regression detection test using historical incident replay harness (small dataset)
notes: Design decision: prefer a focused prompt family set over a large corpus to reduce noise and cost; maintain the mapping in repo for easy edits.
Risk: false positives during model fine-tuning cadence. Mitigation: add short-term smoothing window and require consistent failure across 2 runs before auto-blocking.
Operational: SRE to own the alert runbook; PM to own customer-impact classification for prompt families.
